editorial:
Three generations of the Deetz family are back in Winter River after a family tragedy, and things get wild fast. Lydia is still dealing with her past with Betelgeuse, while her teenage daughter Astrid accidentally opens a door to the Afterlife. The movie mixes spooky fun with family drama, and the vibe is just as weird and colorful as you remember. You get ghosts, crazy creatures, and plenty of laughs along the way, all wrapped in that classic Tim Burton style.

The acting is a big highlight, with Michael Keaton stealing scenes as the chaotic ghost you love to hate. The pacing keeps things moving, though some side plots feel a little crowded and rushed. Still, the practical effects and wild set pieces make it worth your time. If you enjoy spooky comedies with heart, this one is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Astrid and Lydia work together to stop Betelgeuse from marrying Lydia and trapping her in the Afterlife. They use a trick from the handbook to send him back, and the portal closes. The family finally finds peace, and Astrid makes peace with her mom. The twist is that Betelgeuse is not gone forever, hinting he could return again someday.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves spooky comedies and Tim Burton movies.
